description: PROP-D4-exception-logged-and-continues claims to cover REQ-D4 fail-closed (INV-P1 preservation), but the spec never enumerates the SPECIFIC exception classes that must be caught. REQ-D4 says 'raises for any reason' and expects log step `3-dormant-check-error-<Exception>` — but the existing STEP 3 already uses this exact log-step pattern (line 138-139 `step=f"3-health-check-error-{type(e).__name__}"`), so a naive Exception-swallow in the new dormant check will collide/shadow the existing pattern making log-based verification ambiguous. The spec must (a) prescribe a distinct log-step prefix (e.g. `3-dormant-check-error-...`), (b) prescribe whether the exception handler wraps just the pure call, just the sentinel write, or both, and (c) confirm that catching a broad `Exception` does not accidentally suppress a `write_dormant_sentinel` I/O error whose swallowing would silently miss a real dormant state on subsequent ticks. PROP-D4 as written cannot distinguish these cases.

evidence.snippet: REQ-D4 (fail-closed): IF compute_dormant_state() raises for any reason, the dispatcher SHALL log step="3-dormant-check-error-<Exception>" and CONTINUE the tick without writing a sentinel.
